items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: “Blue Rondo a la Turk” by Dave Brubeck

ctx.x: But it was actually his liver or something. And so Carter died. And then not too long ago, Clinton, the bass player, it’s all the original Woody Shaw band, he passed away. So it was like Victor and I still holding up doing what we need to do individually. But that was one of the most incredible musical experiences, and to me Woody, and I’ll say this with no kind of censorship or any kind of limitations, Woody was probably the last major innovator on the trumpet. There are others who play now who are good. But as…
comes to mind is “Blue Rondo a la Turk” by Dave Brubeck. Especially the middle part
